appearance.twig.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17), as Betula papyrifera: branchlets "dark orange color ... during the summer, becoming dull red in their first winter, gradually growing dark orange-brown, lustrous for four or five years and ultimately covered with the white papery bark". Colour chosen by eye for dark orange-brown; `twig_radius` 8 mm, twice the default, for the four or five years before the white bark (inferred).

traits.shade_tolerance.note: FEIS's paper birch review (Betula papyrifera, read 2026-10-16): "Paper birch is shade-intolerant and can regenerate under even-aged silviculture"; it is restricted to openings in older forests.

traits.flowering_months.note: Seed Manual, Betula chapter (printed p. 305): April to June in the middle of the species' range; it has no Pacific Northwest row, and iNaturalist records in the Puget Sound lowlands have no flowering annotations.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Seed Manual, Betula chapter (printed p. 305): ripe in August and September in the middle of the range, and shed from August into the spring; FEIS (Betula papyrifera) says nearly all of it is shed from September to November. So ripe catkins are on the tree from August to November.

traits.height_max_m.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990), Betula papyrifera (Safford, Bjorkbom and Zasada), Growth and Yield: trees in mature stands average 21 m (70 ft) tall, and on the best sites an occasional old tree exceeds 30 m (100 ft). The typical value is that stand average. Sargent (1922, p. 212) says usually 60 to 70 ft.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Betula papyrifera: leaves 6 cm to 10 cm long.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Betula papyrifera occidentalis: petioles about 15 mm long.

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Birch, paper, green: modulus of elasticity 8,100 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.48).

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Birch, paper, green: modulus of rupture 44,000 kPa (clear wood in static bending).

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1, Birch, paper: average moisture content of green wood, heartwood 89% and sapwood 72% of oven-dry mass; stated as a share, the range between them with its middle typical where both are given.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Betula papyrifera (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.52 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 53 records in 5 sources); trunks 0.52, branches 0.51. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.pipe_tip.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B): the twig's and the leaf's pipe radii are scaled together so the stem's diameter at breast height matches the oldest reference size; the fuller crowns of broadleaf revision 11 carry more leaf, so the yearly rings (pipe_rings) are fitted near zero and the pipe model sets the diameter.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Betula, table 3, read): minimum seed-bearing age 15 years. FEIS (Uchytil 1991, read): seed production begins at about age 15. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 10 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a slender tree with a narrow, open crown, alternate oval, toothed leaves and hanging catkins. Not fitted to measurements. Its pipe_tip, pipe_organ and pipe_rings are scaled together (crown calibration, broadleaf revision 9) so that, with the leaf its crown now keeps, its trunk reaches the reference dbh of 25 cm at 40 years again.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 16 m tall and 25 cm across at breast height at 40 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: green leaves; white bark peeling in papery strips. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: slender hanging fruiting catkins 3 to 5 cm long, green going brown. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: catkins in April and May; the fruiting catkins green in summer, brown in August and September, breaking up in the autumn. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): white bark peeling in papery strips round the stem from orange-brown inner bark, with dark horizontal lenticels; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves somewhat smaller and narrower than shade leaves; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.leaf_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 338, Betula papyrifera: leaf shape ovate.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 338, Betula papyrifera: leaf venation pinnate.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
